report:
MRI of right Knee with 
-Locator, SG PD FatSat, SG T2W FS, SG T1W, AX T2W FS, CO T2W FS



> Linear signal intensity in posterior horn of medial meniscus, with extending into the surface, in favor of tear.
  Degeneration of medial and lateral meniscus.
> Wearing of articular cartilage and subchondral bone marrow edema in medial femoral condyle and medial tibial plateau and tibial intercondylar eminance, reflencting osteoarthritis.
> The contour of ACL in a straight line and increase signal intensity inside on F/S T2WI, in favor of grade 1 injury or degeneration.
> The contour of PCL appears to be within normal, no abnormal signal intensity is noted.
> Both medial & lateral collateral ligaments appear to be within normal.
> Joint effusion and suprapatellar bursitis with suprapatellar, lateral and medial plicae; hypertrophy of the synovium, indicative of synovitis.
> A lobulated cystic lesion in medial popliteal fossa between the tendons of the medial head of the gastrocnemius and the semimembranosus muscles, in favor of Baker's cyst. Increased fat stranding over popliteal fossa.
  Increased fat stranding and minimal fluid accumulation located along the pes anserinus, R/O Anserine bursitis

Impression: 
1. Tear of posterior horn of medial meniscus. Degeneration of medial and lateral meniscus.
2. Osteoarthritis of right knee, more severe at medial compartment, with subchondral bone marrow edema.
3. Mild synovitis of right knee with suprapatellar bursitis and patellar plicae; Baker's cyst with perifocal edema over popliteal fossa.
4. Grade 1 injury or degeneration of ACL.
4. Mild aserine bursitis.
Suggest correlation with clinical manifestation

Findings: There is a minor knee effusion. There is degenerate tearing of the posteromedial corner of the medial meniscus. Normal lateral meniscus.  Normal ACL, PCL, MCL and LCL. Normal extensor mechanism. A small prepatellar fluid-filled bursa is noted.  Mild thinning of the medial compartment articular cartilage is noted. Minor fraying of the patellar articular cartilage is also seen. Normal lateral tibiofemoral and trochlear articular cartilage.  
Conclusion: Degenerate tearing of the posteromedial corner of the medial meniscus. Mild medial tibiofemoral and patellar articular cartilage degeneration. Small prepatellar bursitis.

In the medial compartment, there are radial tear at body and horizontal tear at the posterior horn of the medial meniscus. There is no focal chondrosis or chondral injury. 
 The lateral compartment, there is longitudinal vertical tear at the posterior horn of the lateral meniscus. There is no focal chondrosis or chondral injury. 
 The patellofemoral joint, there is focal cartilage delamination at the medial patellar facet. The trochlear cartilage appears congruent without chondral lesion. The medial patellofemoral ligament is intact.  
 In the intercondylar notch, there is chronic complete tear of the anterior cruciate ligament, at mid substance. The posterior cruciate ligament is intact. There is no anterior tibial translation. 
 There is grade II ligamentous sprain (partial tear) (chronic) of the medial collateral ligament, at mid substance (deep and superficial fibers). The posteromedial oblique ligament is intact.  
 The lateral collateral ligament complexes are intact. The popliteofibular ligament is intact. The meniscopopliteal fascicles are intact.  
 The extensor mechanism is normal.  
 No knee effusion is present. The surrounding musculature is normal. There is no fracture or bone contusion.  Focal cartilage delamination at the medial patellar facet.  
  Radial tear at body and horizontal tear at the posterior horn of the medial meniscus. 
  Longitudinal vertical tear at the posterior horn of the lateral meniscus. 
  Chronic complete tear of the anterior cruciate ligament, at mid substance. 
  Grade II ligamentous sprain (partial tear) (chronic) of the medial collateral ligament, at mid substance (deep and superficial fibers).

> MRI of right knee was performed in sagittal, axial and coronal sections.
> Spin echo sequence were used.

> Depression with suspicious of cortical discontinuity at articular surface of posterior lateral tibia plateau with adjacent  bone marrow edema, R/O bone contusion and occult lateral tibial plateau fracture.
> The contour of MCL is not all in a straight line and increase signal intensity inside, in favor of grade 2-3 injury, major involving femoral original site.
> The contour of ACL is not all in a straight line and increase signal intensity inside, in favor of grade 2 injury.
> There are linear high signal intensity in the body and posterior horn of medial meniscus with extension into the surface, in favor of tear of meniscus.
> There are linear high signal intensity in the body, anterior horn and posterior horn of lateral meniscus with extension into the surface, in favor of tear of meniscus.
> Joint effusion and suprapatellar bursitis with suprapatellar plicae; hypertrophy of the synovium, indicative of synovitis.
    A lobulated cystic lesion in popliteal fossa with a small recess of the knee joint capsule lies medially between the tendons of the medial head of the gastrocnemius and the semimembranosus muscles, in favor of Baker's cyst.
> Subcutaneous soft tissue swelling around knee joint, major at infrapatellar region.
> No significant myositis noted at distal thights to proximal legs.
> The contour of PCL and LCL appear to be within normal, no abnormal signal intensity is noted.
> Mild degeneration of knee joint with spur formation; Grade 3 patellar chondromalacia.

Impression:
1. Bone contusion of tibial plateau with R/O occult posterior aspect of lateral tibial plateau fracture.
2. In favor of tear of lateral meniscus and posterior horn of medial meniscus.
3. In favor of grade 2-3 injury of MCL and grade 2 inury of ACL.
4. Synovitis of right knee joint with suprapatellar bursitis and Baker's cyst.
5. Subcutaneous soft tissue swelling around right knee joint, major at infrapatellar region.
Suggest correlation with clinical manifestation.

Obs. Condromalacia de la rótula derecha.

Aumento de señal del LCA que impresiona continuo, hallazgo inespecífico. LCP y ligamentos

normales. Discreto edema las partes blandas de la banda iliotibial y el cóndilo femoral lateral.

discreto edema las partes blandas regionales.
Condropatía lesiones grado 2 del platillo tibial lateral en la región central de la zona de carga del
cóndilo femoral medial.
Condropatía con lesiones grado 4 de la región periférica de la vertiente lateral de la tróclea
femoral. Condropatía con lesiones grado 3 y 4 de la rótula.
Signos de un síndrome de hiperpresión externa y de fricción de la banda iliotibial, correlacionar
con clínica.
Leve tendinosis cuadricipital distal

 The patellofemoral joint, there is focal high grade chondral defect (more than 50% thickness cartilage loss) with subchondral marrow edema and bone cysts (about intact2-intact3 cm) at the medial trochlea (about intact6*1.5 cm) and lateral trochlea (about 1.2*1.2 cm).  -- Diffuse low grade chondrosis along weight-baring medial femoral condyle.

compartimento femorotibial medial.
Condropatía lesiones grado 3 y 4 de la articulación patelofemoral.

aspecto proximal.
Probable bursitis profunda a los tendones de la pata de ganso

MRI LEFT KNEE

INDICATION:? Meniscal injury

Routine MRI of the left knee shows a tiny hairline superior surfacing tear in the body of the medial meniscus. There is linear degenerative signal in the anterior horn of the lateral meniscus but no discrete tear. ACL and PCL are intact. Extensor mechanism intact. Slight ossification distal quads tendon. Collateral ligaments are intact.

No knee joint effusion. Tiny Baker's cyst. Slight fluid is seen in the popliteal fossa between the medial gastrocs and popliteus measuring 5 mm in thickness by 25 mm in width by 42 mm in length. I question the possibility of previous plantaris rupture.

Tricompartmental osteophytes consistent with osteoarthritis. Focal severe chondrosis along the posterior weightbearing aspect of the medial femoral condyle where there is underlying 8 mm focus of bony edema. Severe cartilage loss in the patella with no underlying bone marrow edema. 

IMPRESSION:

Tiny hairline superior surfacing tear in the body of the medial meniscus. Degenerative signal in the anterior horn of the lateral meniscus with no discrete tear.

Tricompartmental degenerative changes with 8 mm focus of bony edema in the medial femoral condyle and severe cartilage denuding throughout the patella.

Complex fluid is seen in the proximal calf, the inferior aspect is not included on this study suspicious for plantaris rupture.

Regelrechte Artikulationsverhältnisse femorotibial und femoropatellar.  Retropatellar anlagebedingter knöcherner Defekt der lateralen Facette mit erhaltenem Knorpelüberzug, ähnlich zur Gegenseite (vgl. VU [DATE]). Diskrete oberflächliche Chondropathie retropatellar sowie femorotibial medial, keine tiefergreifenden Knorpelschäden. Innenmeniskus gering mukoid signalalteriert, keine meniskale Rissbildung. Kreuzbänder intakt, medialer und lateraler Kollateralbandapparat ebenfalls unauffällig. Ansatztendinopathie der Quadrizepssehne mit geringem patellarem Reizödem. Ansonsten homogenes Knochenmarksignal, kein Knochenödem / Bone Bruise. Minimal akzentuierte Gelenkflüssigkeit, gering flüssigkeitsgefüllte Baker-Zyste.

CONSTATATIONS :

Fractures :
Aucune.

Alignement articulaire :
Normal.

Changements dégénératifs :
Arthrose sévère du compartiment articulaire médial avec perte complète du cartilage des surfaces portantes, ostéophytose marginale et œdème osseux réactionnel des deux côtés.
Arthrose légère à modérée du compartiment latéral avec chondropatie proportionnelle et ostéophytose marginale. Chondropatie modérée focale dans la gorge trochléaire, pas de chondropathie rétropatellaire significative ni d'arthrose du compartiment fémoropatellaire.

Signal de la moelle osseuse :
Par ailleurs normal.

Ligament croisé antérieur : Déchirure partielle chronique proximale de grade bas à modéré.
Ligament croisé postérieur : Déchirure partielle chronique de grade bas à modéré au niveau de la partie moyenne.
Ligament médial collatéral : Signes d'entorse chronique de bas grade.
Complexe du ligament collatéral latéral : normal.

Ménisque médial : Macération dégénérative sévère du corps du ménisque avec perte de volume diffuse. Déchirure horizontale oblique du corps à la jonction de la corne postérieure surfaçant distalement. Signes d'un petit fragment déplacé à la jonction corne antérieure - corps vers la gouttière fémorale.
Ménisque latéral : Macération dégénérative avec changements signalatifs internes impliquant la corne antérieure, le corps et la corne postérieure. Signes d'une déchirure dégénérative de bas grade avec une composante horizontale dominante dans le corps du ménisque.

Tendons extenseurs : Normaux.
Rétinacula patellaire : Normales.
Pes anserinus : Normal.

Coin postéro-latéral et postérieur : Enthésopathie dégénérative du tendon semi-membraneux distal.

Épanchement articulaire : Petit épanchement articulaire réactionnel.
Kyste de Baker : Petit kyste de Baker avec des signes de fuite proximale et distale.

Autres trouvailles significatives :
Petit kyste ganglionnaire à la jonction myotendineuse du tendon du poplité.
Varicose veineuse impliquant le creux poplité.

CONCLUSION :
Arthrose tricompartimentale, sévère dans le compartiment médial.
Macération dégénérative des deux ménisques avec déchirures dégénératives, pire au niveau du ménisque médial.
Déchirures chroniques de grade bas à modéré des ligaments croisés antérieur et postérieur.
Petit épanchement articulaire réactionnel et petit kyste de Baker avec signes de fuite.
